To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a widespread 8–10 million years ago tectonic event offshore Costa Rica, as recorded in reflection seismic data and dated by seismic correlations to ODP Site-1039, may be the result of Cocos Ridge-Cocos Plate collision.

(1) The Cocos Ridge collided with the Cocos Plate in the period 9–10 Ma, (2) The collision was facilitated by widespread sill intrusions, (3) The collision was recorded by a series of seismic reflections that correlate with a seismic reflector at the base of a sedimentary sequence, (4) The collision was accompanied by an abrupt change in the magnetic anomaly pattern, and (5) The collision was followed by a set of ridge jumps at 8.
